transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Um... I guess my mind just won't stay on one thing anymore. At work—at the bench—I just kind of jump around. Like, I'll be looking at a customer email, then I'm focused on a saw mark, then some noise outside... and then I realize I've completely lost the work order. So... yeah. That's mostly why I'm here.
Have you always had trouble like this with distractibility since childhood, or did this really start or get noticeably worse only recently?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't thought about it. I guess I just noticed it getting in the way lately... but I don't really know about before.
Thinking back, can you tell me roughly when you first started noticing this trouble staying focused—was it weeks, months, or longer ago?
Um... I'm not really sure. I don't really keep track of that kind of thing. Just... recently, I guess. It's hard to put an exact timeframe on it.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Um... yeah, I guess. The last couple of weeks have been... hard. I just wake up and it's like this heavy, hollow feeling. Like... the shine is just gone out of everything. I don't really know how else to explain it. I've even... um... I've cried in my truck a few times before opening the shop. So, yeah. I guess I have been feeling down.
Did this heavy, down feeling start around the same time as any particular stressful event or change in your life, or did it seem to come on without a clear trigger?
Um... no, not really. Nothing specific happened to set it off. It just... I don't know. This depressed, guilty feeling has just been hanging over me for about a month now. I don't really know why.
Over the past month, have you found yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things, even when there's no clear reason to, and finding it hard to stop or control that worry?
Um... no, not really. I mean, I worry about normal stuff sometimes, like the shop, but... it's not like I can't stop. It's just the sadness mostly.
Over the past month, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Um... yeah. It's been pretty bad. Even if I get in bed at a normal hour, I just... I toss around a lot. And then I end up waking up way before dawn, just... thinking about work stuff. Like a missed delivery at the shop. I don't know. When I finally have to drag myself up, I just... I don't feel rested at all.
Over the past month, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, or that life isn't worth living?

Um... yeah. I guess. It's just... I keep thinking that maybe... maybe my family, or the people who come into the shop, that they'd just be better off if I wasn't here. I don't... I wouldn't actually do anything, I don't have a plan or whatever, but... it's just there a lot. It kind of scares me.

Over the past month, has this affected your ability to keep the shop running and manage your daily responsibilities—are you still able to function at work and at home, or has it become very difficult to carry out even basic tasks?

Um... yeah, I guess it has. Work is... well, it's not great. I missed that big custom delivery I mentioned before. And my records for the shop just got so... disorganized. I actually had to stop taking new work for now. I just can't right now. And, um... my family's been checking in on me a lot more lately. I think they got worried because I've just... really slipped away from my usual routines and stuff.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than normal, and felt like you could take on anything?

Um... yeah, I guess. There was a time... after this one show. I don't really know how to explain it, but I just felt... lit up. Like I was larger than life for a minute. But then... I don't know, I'd just snap at anyone who told me to stick to normal shop hours, or... or asked me to slow down. I just... yeah.
That time you felt 'lit up' and larger than life after the show—about how many days in a row did that feeling last?

Um... I guess... it started right after I got an award at that show. And... it just kept going for a while. Maybe... like two weeks? Yeah, about two weeks of just feeling really wired and out of control.

latest_inference.note: The patient's history of a distinct ~2-week period of elevated, 'lit up,' larger-than-life mood with irritability, decreased need for rest, and impulsivity confirms a prior manic/hypomanic episode.
